transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-03-04
Start time (UTC): 15:00
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Reed (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Samir Khan (CTO, Vantage Labs), Leah Park (ML Engineer), Derrick Wu (Eng Mgr)

Summary (auto): We ran through Redwood's PLG quickstart, time-to-first-token expectations, and higher level infra options (hosted, dedicated, private). Customer wants rapid trial with sample benchmarks and clarity on security & deployment options. Agreed to provide credits and schedule deeper demo.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Reed: Hey everyone thanks for joining, uh this is Alex from Redwood, i'm with Priya our SE. quick agenda - quickstart + credits, time to first token, and then security/deploy options. Samir you wanna kick off with a bit about what you all are trying to do?
[00:18] Samir Khan: Yeah thanks Alex, uh so Vantage Labs we're building an assistant for internal research triage, mostly summary and contextual search over docs. Main asks are like low latency for realtime queries, cost control, and obviously data residency, we we are in the EU so residency matters.
[00:33] Alex Reed: Got it, that's helpful. are you leaning toward a hosted API or do you already have infra requirements that push you to dedicated or private?
[00:45] Leah Park: short term we want the fastest path so hosted is attractive — get tokens flowing quickly. But mid-term we may need dedicated capacity for predictable throughput and maybe a VPC for compliance.
[00:58] Priya Nair: totally makes sense. our PLG quickstart is built exactly for that flow — you can sign up, get free credits, install our SDK or call curl to get your first token within minutes. we also have guides for embeddings and streaming. most teams get to first token in under 10 minutes, to a basic gen or embed.
[01:20] Derrick Wu: under 10 minutes — nice. couple questions: what does the trial include? is there a limit on models? and i imagine no access to dedicated in trial right?
[01:31] Alex Reed: trial includes credits for hosted usage across our model catalog, so you can test curated open models and redwood-verified profiles. dedicated is a reserved capacity product so not part of the self-serve trial, but we can scope a dedicated PoC if you want predictable throughput later.
[01:46] Samir Khan: ok. on security — do you have SOC 2 and what's the SSO story? also we use GCP, any concerns with network egress or region controls?
[01:58] Priya Nair: we are SOC 2 Type II compliant, and have SAML SSO + SCIM for enterprise. for Private deployments we support VPC peering and an on-prem package if you need air-gapped. for Hosted we can restrict region and we have controls for data retention; also we support KMS integrations for encryption at rest in Private and Dedicated options.
[02:20] Samir Khan: when you say data retention controls, can we log-only with no storage? we want ephemeral usage except for explicit logs.
[02:29] Alex Reed: yes, you can set retention policies and there's an option for minimal retention for compliance. we can share the SOC2 and security architecture docs after this call.
[02:38] Leah Park: great — also curious about latency. for us sub-200ms tail matters for short queries. what's realistic on hosted vs dedicated?
[02:47] Priya Nair: depends a lot on model size and sequence length. for smaller models and optimized kernels, hosted can hit 50-150ms p50 on gen requests, but tail latency and throughput will be better with Dedicated where you can pin GPUs and tune batching. we have tools to suggest batching and quantization with Redwood Optimize to balance cost/latency.
[03:08] Derrick Wu: do you support KV cache and prefix caching — we want to avoid repeated context costs with conversational histories.
[03:16] Priya Nair: yes, we do KV cache and prefix caching; sometimes in transcripts that gets called K-V cash, but it's KV cache for the key/value store to re-use attention cache. helps a lot with cost on multi-turn.
[03:29] Samir Khan: funny — i've seen it as cash too. ok on integration, how invasive is SDK? we have a go and python stack.
[03:38] Alex Reed: SDKs for Python, Node, Go (community). the HTTP API is straightforward — token, model, prompt. we'll share quickstart repo and cURL examples in the follow up. time-to-first-token is usually dominated by account signup and grabbing creds, so plan for a 10-30 minute friction window.
[03:56] Leah Park: perfect. one more thing: can we run a benchmark with our 1k token prompts and compare hosted vs dedicated - cost per 1k tokens + p95 latency?
[04:07] Priya Nair: yes that aligns with our usual POC plan — we can spin up a temporary dedicated benchmark if you want, or run on hosted first. recommended path: run on hosted quickstart to validate quality and integration, then do a short dedicated PoC for throughput/latency comparison.
[04:27] Derrick Wu: budget question — how do you price hosted vs dedicated? ballpark numbers help for internal approval.
[04:34] Alex Reed: hosted is usage-based per token / embedding unit. Dedicated is a reserved monthly commitment with predictable throughput pricing. i'll send a short pricing summary in follow up; for a rough ballpark we can share examples from similar customers.
[04:47] Samir Khan: and competitors — what's the practical difference vs OpenAI or Anthropic? are you just a re-seller?
[04:56] Priya Nair: we are a platform for serving and optimizing models — not a single model provider. you can run open models or customers' own models. compared to OpenAI, we offer dedicated/private deployment and more control over routing, caching, and quantization recommendations. vs cloud providers like Vertex, we provide a unified runtime and developer tooling tuned for inference economics.
[05:14] Alex Reed: also worth noting we have Redwood Optimize that surfaces batching and quantization suggestions to cut cost. we often benchmark cost/unit with customers during PoCs.
[05:24] Leah Park: sounds good. what's the timeline for us? we want internal approval in two weeks and a PoC in three to four weeks.
[05:32] Alex Reed: that's reasonable. next steps i propose: we'll send credits + quickstart guide today, Priya will schedule a 60-minute technical sandbox/demo where we'll run your 1k token prompts, and we'll share SOC2 and security docs.
[05:45] Samir Khan: agreed. Leah will own providing example prompts and a small sample dataset. Derrick will own internal procurement gating.
[05:53] Priya Nair: i'll also draft a benchmark plan — p50/p95, cost per 1k tokens, memory utilization for dedicated config. we'll loop in Support for any networking details.
[06:05] Alex Reed: cool. any other blockers? nothing heard so far. if no questions we'll wrap.
[06:12] Leah Park: nup, all good.
[06:14] Derrick Wu: good.
[06:16] Samir Khan: thanks everyone.

Recap (auto): Provide trial credits and quickstart materials; schedule technical sandbox with Redwood SE to run benchmarks; share SOC2/security and pricing summary; customer to provide sample prompts and dataset. Owners assigned.

References/Links: Quickstart repo: https://redwood.ai/quickstart (link shared in chat), SOC2 pack (link to be sent), Pricing one-pager (link to be sent)

End of transcript.
